title: Generic points and selected stalks in a reduced affine injective factorization
statement: Let $R$ and $B$ be reduced commutative rings (no nonzero nilpotent elements), let $u:B\hookrightarrow R$ be an injective unital ring homomorphism, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $h=\operatorname{Spec}u:T\to Y$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $g:Y\to X$ be a morphism to a scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme], and put $f=g\circ h$. Write $T^0,Y^0,X^0$ for the generic points [def-sc-generic-point] of irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Suppose $T^0$ is finite, $f(T^0)\subseteq X^0$, and $f:T^0\to X^0$ is injective. Then $h$ induces a bijection $T^0\to Y^0$, and $g$ maps $Y^0$ injectively into $X^0$. Moreover, for any $t\in T$, $y=h(t)$ and $x=f(t)$, if the composite stalk map $\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\mathcal O_{T,t}$ is an isomorphism, then $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\mathcal O_{T,t}$ is injective and both displayed maps are isomorphisms. These are the stalk maps induced by $g$ and $h$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Empty spectra are allowed.

source.place: Tag 09NI, label lemma-points-in-affine, middle paragraph: the subring R′ of R, generic-point lifting, and the three local rings. Extracted comparison, with the finiteness of T^0 made explicit.

proof.text: We use specialization in the direction $a\leadsto b$ meaning $b\in\overline{\{a\}}$. In an affine spectrum the closure of the prime $P$ is $V(P)$: a closed set $V(I)$ contains $P$ exactly when $I\subseteq P$, which implies $V(P)\subseteq V(I)$. Thus $P\leadsto Q$ means $P\subseteq Q$. The cited component theorem and the definition of generic point identify $T^0$ and $Y^0$ with the minimal primes of $R$ and $B$. We also use that comparable component generic points of $X$ are equal. Indeed specialization gives inclusion of their closures; those closures are maximal irreducible closed subsets, so they coincide, and uniqueness of the generic point in a scheme gives equality. Morphisms preserve specialization by continuity.

source.place: Tags 00ES (algebra-lemma-irreducible), parts (1),(3), and 01IS (schemes-lemma-scheme-sober); preliminary identifications for 09NI.

proof.text: For $Q\in Y^0$, the injective-minimal-prime lifting theorem applied to $u:B\hookrightarrow R$ gives a prime $P\subset R$ with $u^{-1}(P)=Q$. Choose a minimal prime $P_0\subseteq P$ using the prime-contains-minimal-prime theorem. The contraction $u^{-1}(P_0)$ is a prime contained in $Q$, hence equals $Q$ by minimality. Therefore every point of $Y^0$ is the image of some point of $T^0$. This argument does not require finiteness or a generic-point lifting assertion for arbitrary continuous dominant maps.

source.place: Tag 09NI (lemma-points-in-affine), middle paragraph: choosing a generic lift; justified by Tags 00FK (algebra-lemma-injective-minimal-primes-in-image) and 00E0 (algebra-lemma-Zariski-topology), part (4).

proof.text: Let $\eta\in T^0$, and choose a minimal prime $Q\subseteq h(\eta)$ of $B$. Step 2 gives $\eta_0\in T^0$ with $h(\eta_0)=Q$. The specialization $Q\leadsto h(\eta)$ gives $f(\eta_0)\leadsto f(\eta)$. Both points belong to $X^0$ by hypothesis, so Step 1 makes them equal. Injectivity of $f$ on $T^0$ implies $\eta_0=\eta$, whence $h(\eta)=Q\in Y^0$. Together with Step 2 this proves surjectivity $T^0\to Y^0$; injectivity follows immediately from that of $f=g\circ h$. For $\xi\in Y^0$, a lift $\eta$ gives $g(\xi)=f(\eta)\in X^0$. If $g(\xi_1)=g(\xi_2)$, lift both and apply injectivity of $f$ to conclude $\xi_1=\xi_2$.

proof.text: Fix $t$, put $y=h(t)$ and $x=f(t)$, and assume the composite stalk map is an isomorphism. Let $p\subset R$ and $q=u^{-1}(p)\subset B$ represent $t$ and $y$. By the affine-stalk and Spec-map-stalk theorems, identify the two affine stalks with $R_p$ and $B_q$ so that $\beta=h_t^\sharp$ is $b/d\mapsto u(b)/u(d)$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $\alpha=g_y^\sharp:A\to B_q$. The composition theorem identifies $\gamma=f_t^\sharp$ with $\beta\alpha:A\xrightarrow{\sim}R_p$, exactly the assumed composite, without choosing an unrelated local-ring isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09NI (lemma-points-in-affine), middle paragraph: the three displayed local rings; Tags 01HV (schemes-lemma-spec-sheaves), 01I1 (schemes-lemma-morphism-into-affine), and 008M (sheaves-lemma-compose-f-maps-stalks).

proof.text: Write $c_t:\operatorname{Spec}R_p\to T$ and $c_x:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ for the canonical morphisms. Their images are precisely the generalizations of $t$ and $x$. They satisfy $f c_t=c_x\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$. To check this equality, the local-spectrum classification says it suffices to check the closed-point image and its normalized stalk homomorphism: both closed points map to $x$; for $f c_t$ the homomorphism is $f_t^\sharp\!=\gamma$ because $c_t$ has identity normalized stalk map; for $c_x\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ it is again $\gamma$, by the identity normalized stalk map of $c_x$ and the Spec-map-stalk formula (localizing a ring isomorphism at its maximal ideal gives that same isomorphism). Composition of stalk maps supplies both computations. Since $\gamma$ is an isomorphism, so is $\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$. Consequently every generalization $\theta$ of $x$ has a preimage $z\in T$ generalizing $t$ with $f(z)=\theta$: lift $\theta$ along $c_x$, pull back its preimage along $\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, and apply $c_t$.

source.place: Tag 09NI (lemma-points-in-affine), middle paragraph: lifting through the selected stalk isomorphism; Tags 01J6 (schemes-lemma-morphism-from-spec-local-ring), 02NA (schemes-equation-canonical-morphism), and 01J7 (schemes-lemma-specialize-points).

proof.text: Let $Q\subseteq q$ be a minimal prime of $B$, with generic point $\xi\leadsto y$, and let $\eta\in T^0$ be its lift from Step 2. Then $\theta=g(\xi)=f(\eta)$ belongs to $X^0$ and specializes to $x$. Step 5 gives $z\leadsto t$ with $f(z)=\theta$. Choose a minimal prime of $R$ contained in the prime of $z$, giving $\eta'\in T^0$ with $\eta'\leadsto z\leadsto t$. By continuity $f(\eta')\leadsto\theta$. Both are in $X^0$, so they are equal by Step 1. Injectivity on $T^0$ forces $\eta'=\eta$. Thus the minimal-prime lift of $Q$ actually specializes to the prescribed $t$: its prime $P_Q$ satisfies $P_Q\subseteq p$ and $u^{-1}(P_Q)=Q$. This is the specialization assertion not supplied by dominance alone.

proof.text:
We prove $\ker eta=0$. Write $a=b/d\in B_q$ with $d
otin q$ and suppose $ eta(a)=0$. The localization zero criterion gives $s
otin p$ with $s u(b)=0$. For any prime $L\subset B_q$, its contraction $Q'$ to $B$ is prime and contained in $q$, since every element outside $q$ becomes a unit and a proper prime contains no unit. Choose a minimal prime $Q\subseteq Q'$ of $B$. Step 6 supplies $P_Q\subseteq p$ with contraction $Q$. Hence $s
otin P_Q$ and $s u(b)=0\in P_Q$ imply $u(b)\in P_Q$, so $b\in Q\subseteq Q'$. The image $b/1$ lies in $L$, and multiplication by the unit $1/d$ shows $a\in L$. Thus $a$ belongs to every prime of $B_q$. The radical-intersection theorem with $I=0$ says $a$ is nilpotent. The localization of the reduced ring $B$ at $q$ is reduced, so $a=0$. For two elements with equal images apply this to their difference, proving that $ eta$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 09NI (lemma-points-in-affine), middle paragraph: injectivity from minimal-prime lifting; Tag 00E0 (algebra-lemma-Zariski-topology), part (7), and Tag 01HV (schemes-lemma-spec-sheaves), part (6), for the explicit kernel computation.

proof.text: Surjectivity of $\gamma=\beta\alpha$ implies surjectivity of $\beta$: $r=\gamma(c)=\beta(\alpha(c))$ for $c=\gamma^{-1}(r)$. Thus $\beta$ is a ring isomorphism. The map $\alpha$ is injective because $\gamma$ is. For $a\in B_q$, take $c=\gamma^{-1}(\beta(a))$; then $\beta(\alpha(c))=\beta(a)$ and Step 7 gives $\alpha(c)=a$. Hence $\alpha$ is surjective and also an isomorphism. If $T$ is empty, $R$ is the zero ring and injectivity of $u$ forces $B$ to be the zero ring; the generic-point bijection is empty and the stalk assertion has no $t$. The previous arguments already treat all nonempty cases, including generic or closed selected points. The finite-$T^0$ hypothesis is retained, although the injective-ring-map lifting theorem makes it unnecessary in this comparison.
